decisive_join: Recover the enacted Colorado employment ADMT architecture while preserving its 2027 effective boundary and refusing to treat scheduled requirements as operative on the wave date.

findings.claim: Colorado has enacted an employment ADMT governance architecture with distinct developer and deployer custody.
limits: The act's precise application to a named tool, entity, and decision remains fact-specific and may depend on forthcoming rules.

findings.claim: The scheduled deployer transaction includes notice, plain-language explanation, correction, and meaningful human reconsideration rather than a score-only adverse outcome.
limits: The wave does not define the sufficiency of any named explanation or human review.

findings.claim: The enacted record and material-change duties support versioned deployment custody, while the absence of a new private right of action limits what the statute itself authorizes an individual to claim.
limits: Existing rights and remedies outside the act are not adjudicated.

findings.claim: The substantive duties are scheduled for 2027-01-01 and cannot be reported as operative on the wave date.
limits: Rulemaking and transition details remain open.

observations.notes: Colorado enacted and signed the replacement ADMT statute in May 2026.
observations.subject: Colorado SB26-189

observations.notes: The act covers ADMT predictions, rankings, scores, or similar outputs that materially influence consequential decisions, including employment.
observations.subject: Colorado employment ADMT

observations.notes: Developers must provide documentation and material-change information to support deployer compliance.
observations.subject: ADMT developer

observations.notes: Deployers must provide notices, a plain-language adverse-outcome explanation, access and correction, and meaningful human review or reconsideration.
observations.subject: ADMT deployer

observations.notes: The act specifies three-year records, attorney-general enforcement and rulemaking, and no new private right of action.
observations.subject: Colorado ADMT governance
value: no new private right of action

observations.notes: Most substantive developer and deployer duties begin on 1 January 2027 and therefore are not operative on 2026-08-01.
observations.subject: Colorado ADMT duties

selection_rule: Use the enacted bill page and official summary to separate developer documentation, deployer notice, adverse-outcome explanation, access/correction, human review, reconsideration, retention, rulemaking, and private-action limits.

prohibited_inferences: the scheduled duties are operative on 2026-08-01
the act creates a new private right of action
any human involvement satisfies meaningful review
an ADMT score proves the adverse outcome was valid
enactment proves a named employer violated the act

title: Colorado ADMT developer, deployer, explanation, and human-review custody
